story: The Anchorage Assembly passes surveillance ordinance AO 2026-108(S) as amended, 11 to 1, on November 4th. It rejects a 14-day deletion rule in code and a warrant rule for plate searches, adopts a 30-day advance notice rule and creates a temporary APD oversight committee.
stories_surviving: Anchorage Assembly passes AO 2026-108(S) as amended on November 4th after rejecting stricter limits (update of No.84)
'Nobody asked us' data center town hall draws about 150 in Fairbanks (update of No.94)
AEA gets a $32.8 million federal grid resilience formula allocation

claims.claim: The Anchorage Assembly voted 11-1 to pass the administration-backed substitute ordinance AO 2026-108(S) as amended, according to Alaska's News Source.

claims.notes: By Jonson Kuhn, published November 5th at 3:22 PM UTC (6:22 AM AKST). Fetched twice, directly and through r.jina.ai. SINGLE OUTLET. No second outlet reported the final vote. The ADN November 5th committee story says only that members 'continued to clash over Wednesday' on the surveillance rules. The Alaska Public Media Anchorage and public-safety sections, Must Read Alaska and Bing News showed nothing else. No primary source either. Every muni.org Assembly page and PDF returned 404, and meetings.muni.org shows only a search form. KEEP the attribution 'according to Alaska's News Source'. The article doesn't name the lone no vote. The arithmetic checks out for the 12-member Assembly (11+1, and 5+7 on amendments). The version that passed is '(S) as amended', so it is NOT the September 15th (S) text as filed. AI: this source doesn't mention artificial intelligence or machine learning.
